5 - Verify hovering BRAND opens the mega-menu with all 4 brands
FIXED 2026-09-15 — test-side data-drift, not a website bug. ### Root Cause [B] TEST-SIDE ISSUE — same stale-href root cause as test 3 (`a[href='brand.html']` no longer exists), plus a second wrinkle discovered while fixing it: the wrapping `.header-nav-item` div opens the dropdown via its own `x-data="{ open: false }"` + `@mouseenter="open = true"`/`@mouseleave="open = false"` — the BRAND button's `@click="open = !open"` is a secondary toggle on the SAME variable. Retargeting the interaction to `click` (as first attempted) actually broke it: Playwright's click first moves the mouse onto the button (firing `@mouseenter` → open=true), then the click itself fires `@click` and toggles it straight back to false — so `hover` was the correct action all along, just needed retargeting to the real BRAND element instead of the dead `brand.html` anchor. ### Problematic Code `hover: css=a[href='https://nsb-dev.kemanastaging.com/brand.html']` — the anchor no longer exists. ### Fixed Code `hover: xpath=//header[contains(@class,'page-header')]//*[normalize-space()='BRAND']` — same interaction type, retargeted to the real element. ### What To Do No site action needed.

17 - Verify the header remains pinned to the top of the viewport after scrolling
Scrolls to ".benefits-bar", not ".hero" — the hero is the first section on the page, so scrolling "to .hero" from a fresh load never moves scrollY (already in view) and never flips the Alpine "stuck" state that drives the sticky/fixed-header class swap. Confirmed by dumping the header's outerHTML after a .hero scroll_to and seeing the fixed/gradient classes still unapplied. CORRECTED 2026-08-07: the selector used to match on a literal "bg-gradient-to-br" class substring, which the site no longer ships — the gradient is now applied via a Tailwind arbitrary-value class (bg-[linear-gradient(...)]), so the old selector stopped matching anything and this test started failing for a stale-selector reason, not a real regression (confirmed live: the nested header still gets "!fixed" applied on scroll). Switched to a structural selector (header.page-header > header) instead of a specific gradient class name, per the standing lesson to scope by stable structure/attributes rather than bare/arbitrary-value class names.

35 - Verify clicking the 'Trending' Offers filter tab actually filters the product grid
CONFIRMED WORKING (corrected 2026-08-07 — see the "CORRECTIONS" note at the top of this file). This section renders 5 separate x-show-scoped carousels, one per tab; an earlier check queried ".product-card" broadly across the whole section, which silently reads across all 5 hidden+visible carousels at once and made every tab look identical. Playwright's real visibility check (waitFor state: hidden/visible) already respects the x-show-driven display:none on each inactive carousel, so a plain href selector is enough here — no ":visible" pseudo-class needed. FIXED 2026-09-15 — test-side data-drift, not a website bug. ### Root Cause [B] TEST-SIDE ISSUE — the two specific SKUs this step hardcoded ("colorbondr-span-920" for Semua-only, "steel-sample" as a Trending stand-in) have rotated out of the live catalog entirely — this is an actively-developed staging site whose Offers catalog changes over time (same drift pattern already documented in the Compare module). Neither slug exists anywhere in #section-offers anymore, in any tab. ### Problematic Code `css=#section-offers a[href*='steel-sample']` — never existed as a real SKU; a placeholder slug from authoring time. ### Fixed Code Re-verified live which SKUs are actually Semua-only vs Trending-only right now, and swapped in currently-real ones ("zincalume-steel-spandek-optima..." for Semua-only, "bluescope-zacsr-reng" for Trending-only) — the underlying filter behavior being tested is unchanged and still confirmed correct. ### What To Do No site action needed. If this keeps drifting, consider asserting on tab-scoped product COUNT changing rather than specific SKUs, since SKU rotation is expected/ongoing on this catalog.
